cue_frames.caption_text: Open Time reports on the saved deployment.
Choose November second as the report date and select Crew,
with the training community van.
The help explains that there is one report per day for each crew or person, and that
entries are prefilled from the roster.
Select New time report.
A crew scope keeps this exercise focused on the van, its assigned
person and its equipment.
Choose the scope that matches the work you need to document.
The daily report opens as Draft.
Read the Time entries heading: times use the department time zone, America
slash Chicago in this exercise.
The Subject column is prefilled with Matthew Casey, the
training van and Demo radio kit.
Each row initially uses Deployment as Entry type, with an eight o’clock Start.
These are starting values from the roster, so check them against
the actual exercise before saving.
Use the horizontal table scrollbar to reach the remaining columns.
Prepare Casey’s Deployment row with a nine-thirty Start.
Set the van and radio kit rows to nine o’clock.
Use Add entry to create another row, then explicitly choose Casey
as Subject and Travel as Entry type.
Set that travel Start to nine o’clock.
Inspect the new row rather than assuming Add entry selected the
intended person or activity.
This makes travel and coordination separate entries while keeping vehicle
and equipment usage on their own subjects.
Scroll the table right to End, Paid break, Unpaid break, kilometres and Notes.
End the coordination, van and radio entries at one in the afternoon.
End Casey’s travel at nine-thirty.
Enter a ten-minute paid break and a thirty-minute unpaid
break on the coordination row.
Keep the other breaks at zero.
Enter twelve point five kilometres on the van row and add a short note to each row.
The notes distinguish fictional coordination, vehicle
use, radio use and travel.
Use Save in Actions to retain this draft.
Save and submit is a separate control; this exercise uses Save.
Review both sides of the returned table.
Casey’s coordination shows three hours: nine-thirty to one, less
the thirty-minute unpaid break.
The paid break is not subtracted from that displayed total.
Travel shows half an hour, while the van and radio each show four hours.
Read the saved subject choices as well as the numbers so each total stays
attached to the correct resource.
Return to the deployment’s Time reports tab.
Its Summary now shows three point five Personnel hours, representing
Casey’s three hours of coordination and half an hour of travel.
Vehicle and equipment hours are recorded separately; they are not
extra people in that personnel total.
The report list shows the dated crew report as Draft.
Use Open to return to that report.
A saved draft and a submitted or approved report are different states,
so verify the displayed Status before treating it as ready for a later review.
In the report’s Expenses section, enter November second, choose
Fuel, and enter twenty-four dollars and fifty cents in U S D.
Add the training fuel description and Chicago as City.
At Receipt, use Choose File to select the fictional receipt image.
This fixture clearly says that no purchase or payment occurred.
Leave Pre-approved unchecked and clear Billable for this
operational-only exercise.
Check those choices before selecting Add expense, because the form is preparing a
new expense, not changing an existing one.
After Add expense, the report lists Fuel, its training
description and the saved amount.
Return to the deployment’s Expenses tab for another readback.
The row shows November second, Chicago, twenty-four dollars and
fifty cents, and Not billable.
Its Time report link is number two, tying this expense to the daily report.
Total is also twenty-four dollars and fifty cents.
The Receipt column offers the attachment; the downloaded file in this exercise
matches the uploaded test receipt.
Use this process for the people, vehicles and equipment in your own department.
Community paramedicine and mental health response teams, search-and-rescue teams,
security companies, wildland contractors and industrial emergency teams can
document assignment time and expenses alongside fire and E M S departments.
Choose the right report scope, verify the time zone, and inspect
saved hours and expense links.
This example ends with a draft and a fictional nonbillable expense;
later submission and approval require their own completed review.
